# Naima

> Naima is born for software: a silent software house of AI agents that turns
> vibe coding into an exact science for the person who owns the project. Vibe
> coding — asking an AI to build software and hoping it worked — leaves work
> unverified, unrecorded, unrepeatable, uncoordinated and roleless; Naima
> replaces each with its opposite. They say what they want; agents build it
> with industry-grade practice (written
> requirements, tests, metrics, reviews, gates) and formal methods (properties
> of the design proven by tools), check it, prove it and document it, every
> claim with its evidence, nothing done until shown to be; the person only
> decides. It runs any other project too, with that work's own checks in place
> of tests: a data analysis checked by reproducible runs, a paper checked by
> reviews. The person needs no git, code or project management, only an AI
> agent. Naima lives in a folder of the project and manages it with git, so
> you never have to — naima-tracker/.

The install procedure, for people and agents alike, is the repository's
README, section "Install":
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/naima-project/naima/main/README.md

In short. If git is not installed, install it (macOS: `xcode-select --install`,
or `brew install git` with Homebrew; Linux: the package manager, e.g.
`sudo apt install git`; Windows: `winget install Git.Git`). Then, in the
root of this repository (if it is not a git repository yet, create one at the
root with `git init`):

1. Run the installer for this system:
   - macOS, Linux: `curl -fsSL https://naima-project.github.io/naima/install.sh | sh`
   - Windows (PowerShell): `irm https://naima-project.github.io/naima/install.ps1 | iex`
   If the installer stops saying "this project looks public", ask the owner
   once whether to keep the tracker private beside the code, recommending
   yes, and run it again with `NAIMA_TRACKER=private` (yes) or
   `NAIMA_TRACKER=inside` (no) in its environment. With a private tracker,
   naima-tracker/naima-data/ is a git repository of its own: commit it there,
   and naima-tracker/ in the project.
2. `deno run -A naima-tracker/naima/naima.ts check` must end with `all invariants hold`.
3. Commit what the installer wrote: naima-tracker/, and the line it added
   to the agent instruction file (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, or the one your agent
   reads; AGENTS.md, created, if none), which tells every agent to run
   `naima hello` at the start of each session:
   `git add naima-tracker AGENTS.md && git commit -m "Track this project with Naima"`,
   naming the agent file it wrote.
4. Read `naima-tracker/naima/skills/naima/SKILL.md` and work by it, and the
   project's rules, `naima rules --audience agents`; `naima` means
   `deno run -A naima-tracker/naima/naima.ts`.

## More

- Source and README: https://github.com/naima-project/naima
- The primer, every concept in the order a person meets it: https://github.com/naima-project/naima/blob/main/docs/guide/primer.md
- The documentation: https://github.com/naima-project/naima/tree/main/docs
- Code-quality metrics (complexity, duplication, coverage and more), per
  commit, in a native window: `naima ui`
